subject.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose these five memory roles, per-agent role overrides, and memoryRole hook metadata as the core plugin/config contract?
rationale: The branch is technically coherent but creates durable public config and plugin SDK surface, chooses role names before every role has a complete invocation protocol, and defines a legacy compatibility window that code review cannot authorize without product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor the role contract
options.body: Approve the five-role taxonomy and per-agent model, then require a clean rebase, explicit legacy migration policy, and current-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the first contract
options.body: Ship only roles with complete runtime protocols now and defer dreaming, userModel, or other provisional roles until their invocation contracts are specified.

options.title: Continue through the RFC
options.body: Pause this implementation and settle the taxonomy and compatibility policy in https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/22 before refreshing a smaller implementation PR.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the role contract
recommendation.body: Approve the five-role taxonomy and per-agent model, then require a clean rebase, explicit legacy migration policy, and current-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory plugin-host architecture and public config/plugin boundaries trace most strongly to their prior refactors.
